sources.citation: Greenhill, Simon J. (ed.) TransNewGuinea.org, language page 'Sonia' (transnewguinea.org/language/sonia, fetched sources 2026-09-17)
sources.note: 97-item lexicon, sole source Shaw (1986); phonetic forms without stress marks; alt name 'Sunia'.

sources.citation: Pawley, Andrew & Harald Hammarstrom. 2018. The Trans New Guinea family. In Bill Palmer (ed.), The Languages and Linguistics of the New Guinea Area: A Comprehensive Guide, 21-195. Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton. (OAPEN open-access chapter via Internet Archive item oapen-20.500.12657-23719)
sources.note: Nothing on Sonia prosody; p.37 documentation census reads 'Sonia [siq] 400; wordlist: Shaw 1986', i.e. confirms wordlist-only documentation; notes Kaluli and Sunia share 70% lexicostatistical similarity and probably form a subgroup.

sources.citation: Shaw, R. Daniel. 1986. The Bosavi language family. In D. Laycock et al. (eds), Papers in New Guinea Linguistics No. 24, 45-76. Pacific Linguistics A-70. Canberra: ANU. DOI 10.15144/PL-A70.45
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 1.1 'Phonological data' and Table 1 (p.48) give a partially phonemicised inventory for Sunia with supra-segmentals listed only as nasalisation, vowel length and closed syllables; the words stress/accent/tone do not occur in the paper, and the Appendix Swadesh-100 Sunia list carries no stress marks. Author calls the analysis 'cursory' and 'preliminary at best'.
